data.description:
## Context
Split from ea66 (closed as not_a_bug on 2026-10-25: its three metrics were measured publishing on 2026-09-20 and 2026-10-24, with datapoints in 168 of 168 hours). The 2026-09 silence was never diagnosed, and nothing today distinguishes a metric that stopped publishing from one reporting a bad value or one whose name is merely still listed. CloudWatch `list-metrics` keeps a metric name long after its datapoints stop, so name presence proves nothing.

The three alarms on `disk_used_percent{mount=/var/gerrit}`, `gerrit_healthy` and `reviewbot_healthy` use `treat_missing_data = breaching`, so a silent publisher already puts them in ALARM. This task is the broader capability: enumerate and detect the class rather than discover it during an incident.

## Constraint
Per the `project.portability` plan-review criterion the detector must run in-process or be operation-linked, not depend on one CI provider's scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A metric that stops publishing is detected distinctly from a bad value and from an absent name (checked: a test or drill that stops a publisher, with the detection output recorded).
- [ ] The check asserts on datapoint recency over a defined window and never on `list-metrics` name presence (checked: the test fails if the check is switched to name presence).
- [ ] An audit of all `rebar/host` metrics states which are live, recorded in the tree.
- [ ] The detector fails loudly if it stops running (checked: a test where the detector does not run reports failure, not success).
- [ ] `make verify` shows no failure outside the known pandoc set, and the Gerrit change is `Verified +1`.

## Non-goals
Not the `/var/gerrit` mount assertion (`unamused-cloudy-junebug`), not off-box log shipping (`fab-dismal-haddock`), not `treat_missing_data` (`herbal-garish-monkey`).
data.title: Detect rebar/host metrics that stop publishing, by datapoint recency
